title: Deploy and test a model · Level 3
slo: Configure a deployed model and test it in the Foundry playground.

options.text: A smallest unit of text or data
options.rationale: A token is a smallest unit of text or data a model processes. It can be a word, subword, character, or punctuation.
RPM counts requests per minute. Tokens are units within processed text or data.
options.better_fit: Use this idea when discussing request count per minute.

feedback.intrinsic: Message count could be confused with text size.
feedback.instructional: Tokens are processed text or data; RPM counts requests.

options.rationale: A selected release is a model version. A token is a unit processed by the model.
options.better_fit: Use this when naming a particular model release.

feedback.intrinsic: Model identity could be confused with data usage.
feedback.instructional: Versions identify releases; tokens measure processed text or data.

options.rationale: Instructions guide behavior and role. Tokens are units of data processing.
options.better_fit: Use this when defining role, tone, or guardrails.

feedback.intrinsic: Behavior could be configured without understanding token use.
feedback.instructional: System instructions guide behavior; tokens are processed units.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Tokens are small units of text or data.

exercises.question_text: Which can a system prompt set? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A system prompt can set the assistant's behavior. It establishes how the assistant should operate.
A system prompt can define tone. Tone guides how responses are expressed.
A system prompt can establish tools and guardrails. These guide capabilities and boundaries.
Max output tokens sets the response-length cap. A system prompt instead sets behavior-related guidance.
options.better_fit: Use this when setting a firm maximum response length.

feedback.intrinsic: Behavior may be specified while replies remain longer than intended.
feedback.instructional: Use max output tokens for length and a system prompt for behavior guidance.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A system prompt can set behavior, tone, tools, and guardrails.

exercises.question_text: The Foundry playground is used only after all application code is written.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The team could build around untested prompts.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use the playground to test prompts, compare models, and capture settings before writing code.

exercises.explanation: Correct. It helps test prompts and settings before coding.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the setting and processing would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place the deployment setting first, then state what it determines.

exercises.correct_answer: Deployment type determines where and how inference is processed for a workload.
exercises.explanation: Deployment type is the subject, followed by its effect on inference processing.

exercises.question_text: The prompt that establishes an assistant's behavior and role is the ___.

parts.text: The prompt that establishes an assistant's behavior and role is the

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The prompt type would be mislabeled.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use a system prompt for behavior guidance and a user prompt for the end user's request.

exercises.explanation: A system prompt establishes behavior and role, unlike a user prompt, which states an end user's request.

exercises.question_text: A company has throughput and data-processing requirements for an AI service. Which decision best addresses those requirements?

options.rationale: Deployment type is connected to throughput and data-processing requirements. It therefore best addresses the stated constraints.
A model version identifies a release. It does not address the deployment processing arrangement.
options.better_fit: Use this when compatibility requires a particular model release.

feedback.intrinsic: The service could have a release selected but no solution for processing requirements.
feedback.instructional: Match throughput and data-processing needs to deployment type.

options.rationale: Temperature changes response variation. It does not determine the processing configuration.
options.better_fit: Use this when creative variation versus repeatability is the issue.

feedback.intrinsic: Output style could change without addressing capacity requirements.
feedback.instructional: Temperature affects response behavior; deployment type addresses processing needs.

options.rationale: Instructions guide assistant behavior and guardrails. They do not choose a deployment arrangement.
options.better_fit: Use this when role, tone, or safety guidance must change.

feedback.intrinsic: The assistant may behave differently while deployment requirements remain unmet.
feedback.instructional: Deployment type, not instructions, addresses processing requirements.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Deployment type is the decision linked to throughput and data processing.

exercises.question_text: To test prompts and capture working settings before coding, use the Foundry ___.

parts.text: To test prompts and capture working settings before coding, use the Foundry

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected tool would not provide the intended interactive testing workspace.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use the playground for prompt testing; use the catalog for discovery and APIs for code calls.

exercises.explanation: The Foundry playground is the portal interface for testing prompts and settings.

exercises.question_text: Which statements about token and request limits are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: TPM limits token traffic per minute
options.rationale: TPM is an allocation and rate limit for token traffic per minute. It measures token capacity over time.
RPM limits how many requests can be handled per minute. It counts requests rather than tokens.
Temperature controls response variation. RPM controls request count per minute.
options.better_fit: Use temperature when adjusting creativity or repeatability.

feedback.intrinsic: Busy-period request limits would remain unchanged.
feedback.instructional: Use RPM for request count and temperature for variation.

options.rationale: Model version identifies a release. TPM limits token traffic per minute.
options.better_fit: Use model version when selecting a particular release.

feedback.intrinsic: Release identity would be confused with traffic capacity.
feedback.instructional: TPM is the token-traffic limit, not a version label.

exercises.explanation: Correct. TPM concerns token traffic and RPM concerns request count.

exercises.question_text: What does max output tokens set?

options.rationale: Max output tokens sets a cap on response length. It also affects token consumption and can affect throttling.
Temperature controls creative variation and repeatability. Max output tokens controls length.
options.better_fit: Use this when adjusting creativity versus consistency.

feedback.intrinsic: Reply style may change while length remains uncontrolled.
feedback.instructional: Use max output tokens for length and temperature for variation.

options.rationale: RPM limits requests per minute. Max output tokens caps each response's length.
options.better_fit: Use this when controlling request count per minute.

feedback.intrinsic: Response size may change while request rate remains unchanged.
feedback.instructional: Keep per-response length separate from request rate.

options.rationale: Instructions set behavior and role. Max output tokens is a response-length setting.
options.better_fit: Use this when setting role, tone, or guardrails.

feedback.intrinsic: The role may change while answer length remains unchanged.
feedback.instructional: Use instructions for behavior and max output tokens for length.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Max output tokens caps response length.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The directional relationship between temperature and variation would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with higher temperature, then connect it to more creative variation.

exercises.correct_answer: Higher temperature generally favors more creative variation in responses.
exercises.explanation: Temperature balances variation and repeatability; moving it higher favors the variation side of that balance.

exercises.question_text: Max output tokens sets the assistant's behavior, tone, tools, and guardrails.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A team could adjust length when it intended to define behavior.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use system instructions for behavior, tone, tools, and guardrails; use max output tokens for response length.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Instructions set those elements; max output tokens caps length.

exercises.question_text: Which setting controls creativity versus more repeatable responses?

options.rationale: Temperature controls the balance between creative variation and repeatability. It is the relevant setting for this choice.
Max output tokens caps response length. It does not set response variation.
options.better_fit: Use this when replies need a maximum length.

feedback.intrinsic: Replies may shorten without becoming more consistent.
feedback.instructional: Use temperature for variation and max output tokens for length.

options.rationale: Instructions set behavior, role, and guardrails. They do not control the variation balance.
options.better_fit: Use this when defining how the assistant should behave.

feedback.intrinsic: A new role may be set while variation remains unchanged.
feedback.instructional: Instructions guide behavior; temperature governs variation.

options.rationale: TPM is token-traffic capacity per minute. It does not control creativity or repeatability.
options.better_fit: Use this when changing token-traffic capacity.

feedback.intrinsic: Capacity may change without changing answer consistency.
feedback.instructional: TPM manages capacity; temperature manages variation.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Temperature controls creativity versus repeatability.
